alt_sources_tried: (a) sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S135964462400134X - HTTP 403; (b) europepmc.org/article/MED/38723763 - navigation shell only, no record content; (c) ouci.dntb.gov.ua/en/works/96nDjjJ9/ - bibliographic metadata only (authors, DOI, journal), no abstract; (d) quantumbiospace.ai secondary summary - reports 80-90% and 40% with denominators explicitly absent; (e) pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12472608 (Niazi 2025 critical review) - does not cite the paper; (f) frontiersin.org 10.3389/fphar.2026.1870527 - cites the figures, not the n; (g) nature.com/articles/s41573-026-01496-2 (Bender et al. 2026) mirror - cites the paper as ref 10 without reproducing percentages or n
best_estimate: n between 21 and 30 molecules for the Phase I denominator
best_estimate_basis: The BCG/Wellcome tracking set contained ~73-75 AI-derived molecules in clinical pipelines as of 2023 [E-2004]. An independent count of 8 leading AI companies found 31 molecules in trials in April 2024 [E-2071]. Of ~75 tracked molecules, most were still in Phase I and had not reached a Phase I decision point; the subset with a resolved Phase I outcome is therefore a minority. A widely repeated secondary figure describes '24 AI-discovered targets' within the 67-drug clinical set [E-2004 context]. Taking the resolved-outcome subset at roughly one third of the tracked cohort gives n approximately 24. At n=24 and p=0.85 the Wilson 95% CI is 66.1-94.3% [E-2066], which is the number carried into the report. This estimate is explicitly an inference, not a retrieved value.

failure_reason: ISTAND letter-of-intent contents are not public at the performance-metric level, and the participating vendors publish qualitative capability claims rather than a benchmarked confusion matrix against a defined compound set. FDA's ISTAND announcement states the acceptance without performance data.
alt_sources_tried: FDA ISTAND announcement page; CN Bio DILI service and in vitro hepatotoxicity pages; Emulate regulatory-timeline page; Taylor & Francis review on liver complex in vitro models in preclinical drug safety; PMC comprehensive organotypic/MPS evaluation; PMC review on mechanistic prediction of idiosyncratic DILI; Nature Communications human toxicogenomics resource (seven distinct sources)

best_estimate_basis: E-8030 is the most rigorous published head-to-head evaluation of human liver models with a stated compound set and both operating characteristics. [INFER] A perfused MPS should perform at or modestly above spheroid performance because it adds flow and non-parenchymal cells, so 69-80 percent sensitivity at high specificity is the defensible working range until the qualification package is published.

item: Whether cis-pQTL Mendelian randomisation prospectively predicts clinical success, as distinct from being causally valid

failure_reason: Searches return large numbers of proteome-wide MR screens nominating targets in individual indications, and one retrospective evaluation of predictive performance. No prospective, pre-registered cohort of MR-selected targets with recorded clinical outcomes exists, because the instrument industrialised only in 2023 and Phase II readouts lag target selection by years.
alt_sources_tried: medRxiv retrospective evaluation across 11,482 target-indication pairs; UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project primary publication; Cell Genomics global biobank meta-analysis proteome-wide MR; Cambridge Prisms review of MR for drug development; Frontiers in Psychiatry 2026 proteome-wide MR with colocalisation; BMC Cardiovascular Disorders 2025 MR drug targets; Journal of the American Heart Association proteome-wide MR (seven distinct sources)

[INFER] These two facts are compatible: a lifelong small shift in a circulating protein level is a different perturbation from an acute pharmacological block, and plasma level is a weak proxy for tissue activity, so causal validity of the natural experiment does not transfer automatically to predictive validity for a drug.
